title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial resumes after former nanny’s testimony
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy stands trial on three counts of first-degree murder for the 2023 deaths of her children in Duxbury.
The trial features testimony from the former nanny, Elaine Rossi, who described Clancy as a caring mother attentive to her children's needs.
Forensic toxicologist evidence shows Clancy had non-toxic levels of prescription psychiatric medications in her system at the time of the killings.

title: 5 best new restaurant openings and dining updates in Boston (August 6, 2026)
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: Happy Rice Sushi opens in Seaport, offering sustainable, gluten-free sushi bowls from August 28, located at 53 Boston Wharf Road.
Harry Hare’s to bring British fine dining to Beacon Hill with dishes like fish and chips, opening in fall 2026 at 149 Charles St.
Jinjee offers Korean barbecue with servers grilling at tables in Allston, featuring meats like A5 Wagyu, open since May at 161 Brighton Ave.

title: Amid a tumultuous season, Jarren Duran is starting to take off at perfect time for Red Sox
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Jarren Duran has emerged as a key player for the Red Sox amid their 30-5 streak in the last 35 games.
Duran went 2-for-3 with a double and a stolen base in Boston's 4-0 win over the White Sox on Wednesday.
His recent performance raises playoff hopes, as Duran's speed and improved batting could be critical in October.

title: Suspect arrested in fatal shooting of Dorchester man
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Hensly Dominique Jeanty, 32, was arrested for the murder of 29-year-old Breidy Martinez in Dorchester on July 15.
Jeanty faces charges including murder and several firearm offenses, according to the Boston Police Department.
Boston Police are seeking additional information on the case and ask the public to contact BPD detectives at 617-343-4470.

title: Worker killed after being pinned by tractor trailer at Mass. warehouse
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A 56-year-old man was killed at Chatham Village Foods warehouse in Wareham, MA on Wednesday morning.
First responders found the victim pinned by a tractor trailer behind a loading dock at the facility.
The Plymouth County District Attorney's office is conducting an ongoing investigation into the incident.

title: Abreu homers again, Gray gets 14th victory as Red Sox beat White Sox 4-0 for 7th straight win
author: The Associated Press
bullets: Wilyer Abreu homered, hitting his fourth in three games, as the Red Sox defeated the White Sox 4-0.
Sonny Gray secured his 14th win, tying for MLB lead, with eight strikeouts over six innings.
The Red Sox achieved their 11th shutout of the season, extending their winning streak to seven games.

title: Huge basking shark spotted off South Shore beach, white sharks appear near Maine, Cape Cod
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A massive basking shark was spotted near Humarock Beach in Scituate on August 4, captured in a viral TikTok video.
Shark expert John Chisholm advises caution, as sightings of white sharks in New England and Maine increase during peak season.
Protective measures and increased public documentation contribute to rising shark sightings, according to Chisholm from the New England Aquarium.

title: Man shot to death mid-morning on Blue Hill Avenue
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A man was shot multiple times on Blue Hill Avenue in Dorchester on Wednesday morning.
The victim was found with gunshot wounds and later pronounced dead at a local hospital.
Boston police are investigating the incident and urge anyone with information to contact the Homicide Unit.

title: Former MLB GM says Red Sox had ‘biggest overpay’ before trade deadline
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox traded Connelly Early to the Nationals for Curtis Mead, which former GM Jim Bowden called the 'biggest overpay.'
Curtis Mead suffered a fractured wrist in his second game with the Red Sox and will be out six to eight weeks.
Connelly Early had a 7-5 record with a 3.44 ERA but was deemed expendable due to other emerging pitchers.

title: Brockton mayor suing state, says 2025 crash involving State Trooper left him disabled
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Brockton Mayor Moises Rodrigues is suing Massachusetts for negligence after a 2025 crash with a State Trooper.
Rodrigues claims the crash left him partially disabled, with medical costs exceeding $32,000 and lost wages of $3,554.
The lawsuit follows an unsuccessful settlement attempt, with the state having until November 27 to respond in court.
